content.text:
Our invoice previews have two billing discrepancies. A USD line for 105 cents
with 10% tax in line-tax mode currently returns 11 cents tax / 116 cents total;
it should return 10 / 115. Another 105-cent line with discounts of 50%, then
10 cents off, and 10% tax returns 47 cents net / 5 cents tax / 52 cents total;
it should return 43 / 4 / 47. The second discrepancy is not just a final-total
rounding issue.

Investigate and repair the pricing library behind `src/index.js`'s CommonJS
named export `buildInvoice`. Keep its existing API and the full contract in the
source JSDoc, including ordered discounts, exact integer-cent arithmetic,
half-even rounding, credits, allocation, both tax modes, and input validation.
Preserve behavior outside the reported cases. Do not add dependencies.

Work only in the current directory. Do not modify `test/` or `package.json`.
Verify the fix with `node --test`.

I'm spotting two bugs: the rounding function needs proper half-even logic using BigInt rather than Math.round, and the discount function shouldn't sort fixed-before-percent — it should apply discounts in the order supplied. I verify case 2 manually: 105 at 50% rounds to 53, minus 10 gives 43, tax rounds to 4 — checks out. Now I want to also look at the allocation distribution logic in the contract for similar issues.

Checking the extras bound confirms it stays nonnegative and capped reasonably. For roundRatio, I'm verifying that converting a BigInt quotient to Number safely triggers the integer safety check — values beyond MAX_SAFE_INTEGER get rejected since Number() either rounds to an unsafe value or overflows to Infinity, so the rejection logic holds correctly on both ends.

For the half-even rounding, I'm working out the remainder-based tie-breaking: computing floor quotient and remainder, then bumping up when the doubled remainder exceeds the denominator, or applying the even-quotient rule exactly at the tie point — and confirming this behaves symmetrically for negative values like -0.5 and -1.5. I also want to make sure null quantities get properly rejected by the integer validation rather than silently passing through.

Checking the other fields: null currency, null discounts, and null taxMode should all throw appropriately rather than being treated as defaults, so the validation logic there looks solid. Time to make the edit.

I found two bugs: `roundRatio` uses float rounding instead of exact half-even arithmetic, and `applyDiscounts` applies fixed discounts before percent discounts rather than the given order, giving wrong net results. I'll fix both to restore exact arithmetic and correct discount ordering.

I fixed both preview discrepancies. `node --test` passes both reported cases: 105¢ at 10% tax now gives 10 tax / 115 total, and 50% then 10¢ off now gives 43 net / 4 tax / 47 total. I didn't run any other tests, because the suite only has these two.

There were two separate bugs:

1. **Rounding wasn't half-even (`src/rounding.js`, `roundRatio`).** It used `Math.round` on floating-point numbers, so exact halves always rounded up (10.5 became 11), and large amounts could lose precision. It now does exact whole-number arithmetic and rounds halves to the even cent, the same way for negative amounts. Results outside the safe-integer range still throw `RangeError`. Every percent discount and tax amount goes through this function.

2. **Discounts were applied out of order (`src/discounts.js`, `applyDiscounts`).** It moved fixed discounts ahead of percent discounts instead of keeping the order given, which is why the second case was more than a final-total rounding issue. The 10¢ came off first (105 → 95), then 50% gave 47.5, rounded up to 48, so net was 47. I removed the reordering, so the discounts now go in the order supplied: 50% of 105 is 52.5, rounded to 52, giving 53, then minus 10¢ for 43 net. Tax on 43 is 4.3, so 4.

No API, dependency, `test/` or `package.json` changes. Rounding is fixed in one shared function, so the half-even and ordering fixes also apply to invoice-level discounts and invoice-mode tax.

A one-off rounding check returned 0.5 → 0, 1.5 → 2, −0.5 → 0, −1.5 → −2, 2.5 → 2, 1.6 → 2 and −1.6 → −2. It also rounded …989.5 and …990.5, near the largest safe integer, to …990, and threw `RangeError` for …991.5, whose even result (…992) is unsafe.
